findings.quote: I used the lost speed fraction as the ratio
findings.note: Too close to mistakes[0].route ('I took the speed fraction as the distance ratio'): the only thing separating them is the word 'lost', and a student who took some speed fraction as the distance ratio will not reliably remember whether it was the fraction kept or the fraction lost. Two routes a student cannot tell apart break the tap.
findings.fix: I used the speed lost as the distance ratio

notes: Physics re-derived: a = 5u squared over 18x, x' = 4x/5, so 4/5 is right; the three entries' 2/3, 1/3 and 4/9 all reproduce and each route describes its own entry with no option value spelled out. Considered and did not file: right_route (I used the same equation for both stages) never names the equation, which is slightly vague, but the two-stage move is the real identity of the method and it separates cleanly from all three wrong routes, which are all 'I read a ratio straight off'.
